hero.title: Foreign Accounts: Gupta Age
hero.description: Comprehensive analysis of Chinese travelogues, specifically Faxian, providing a contemporary lens into the socio-economic and religious fabric of the Gupta Empire.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Key timelines marking the arrival and stay of foreign observers during the Gupta reign.

cards.details: Faxian (Fa-Hien) traveled across the Gupta territories during the reign of Chandragupta II, primarily focusing on Buddhist sites.

items.title: F-C-G
items.decryption: Remember the sequence: The Chinese pilgrim Faxian (F) visited during the reign of Chandragupta II (C) of the Gupta (G) era.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Faxian NEVER mentions the name of the king (Chandragupta II) in his accounts; he only records his experience of the administration.
Faxian's focus was purely religious (Buddhism); do not expect detailed political accounts like those found in Megasthenes' Indika.
Confusing Faxian (5th Century) with Xuanzang (7th Century - Harshavardhana period).

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Master the key concepts and dimensions of this topic.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centralized around Magadha and Pataliputra.
  • Description of the Ganges valley civilization.

Personalities

  • Faxian: Buddhist monk and explorer.
  • Chandragupta II: The ruling emperor.

Mindmap: Key Observations

  • Socio-Economic State
    • 'Chandalas' existence outside city gates (untouchability).
    • Mild administrative justice system.
    • General prosperity and use of Cowrie shells for trade.
  • Religious Landscape
    • Flourishing of Mahayana and Hinayana Buddhism.
    • Presence of free hospitals and charity inns.
ObserverPeriodPrimary Focus
Faxian405-411 CEPilgrimage & Buddhist texts

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following Chinese pilgrims visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)?
opts: Xuanzang
Faxian
Yijing
Song Yun
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian (Fa-hien) was the first Chinese pilgrim to visit India, arriving during the reign of Chandragupta II around 399-414 CE. Xuanzang visited during Harshavardhana's reign, while Yijing came later in the 7th century.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary objective of Faxian's journey to India?
opts: To establish diplomatic trade relations between China and the Gupta Empire
To search for and collect authentic Buddhist texts and scriptures
To conquer Indian territories on behalf of the Chinese Emperor
To study Hindu temple architecture and mathematics
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian undertook the perilous journey from China to India primarily out of a deep devotion to Buddhism, seeking genuine Vinaya Pitaka texts and other Buddhist scriptures that were missing or corrupted in China.

practiceQuestions.q: By what title or name is Faxian's famous travelogue commonly known in historical literature?
opts: Si-Yu-Ki (Records of the Western Regions)
Fo-Kuo-Ki (A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms)
Memoirs of the Middle Kingdom
Nan-Hai-Chi-Gui (A Record of Buddhist Practices)
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian wrote his travelogue under the title 'Fo-Kuo-Ki', meaning 'A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms'. 'Si-Yu-Ki' is the work of Xuanzang, and 'Nan-Hai-Chi-Gui' was written by Yijing.

practiceQuestions.q: Approximately how many years did Faxian spend traveling inside India during his mission?
opts: About 2 years
About 6 years
About 15 years
About 20 years
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian left China in 399 CE, reached India and spent about 6 years traveling across various Buddhist sites within the subcontinent, and finally returned to China by sea in 414 CE, taking around 15 years for the entire round trip.

practiceQuestions.q: According to Faxian, what was the administrative condition of the penal system and governance in the Madhyadesha (Gupta heartland)?
opts: Extremely harsh with frequent capital punishment and torture
Mild and lenient, with fines imposed even for major crimes rather than corporal punishment
Non-existent, as local guilds managed all law and order
Dictated entirely by strict Buddhist monastic codes
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian noted that the administration of the Gupta Empire was benevolent and light-handed. For minor offenses, only fines were levied, and even for repeat treason, the standard punishment was merely the amputation of the right hand rather than death.

practiceQuestions.q: Which important city did Faxian describe as having grand charitable institutions, free hospitals, and flourishing Buddhist centres?
opts: Ujjain
Mathura
Pataliputra
Valabhi
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian was deeply impressed by Pataliputra, where he described Asoka's palace as being built by spirits (gods) and praised the free hospitals endowed by benevolent householders and nobility for the poor and destitute.

practiceQuestions.q: What did Faxian report regarding the medium of exchange and currency usage in daily transactions within the Gupta Empire?
opts: Gold coins were used exclusively by all citizens for buying vegetables and food.
Cowrie shells were widely used as the common currency for small-scale retail trade.
A strict barter system with no circulating money was enforced by the state.
Paper currency backed by the imperial treasury was standard.
practiceQuestions.sol: While the Guptas issued magnificent gold coins (dinaras) for high-value trade and royal functions, Faxian observed that cowries (shells) served as the primary medium of exchange in everyday market transactions for common people.

practiceQuestions.q: According to Faxian's observations, which social community or caste was generally exempted from royal restrictions and physical constraints while travelling freely across the country?
opts: Kshatriyas
Vaishyas and merchants
Buddhists and general travelers without registration
There was no widespread system of police registration or internal passports for anyone.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian noted that people were free to travel without registering their movements or obtaining passports, reflecting an exceptionally relaxed administrative apparatus where citizens could move in and out of towns without obstruction.

practiceQuestions.q: What observation did Faxian make regarding vegetarianism and dietary habits among the general populace in the Gupta realm?
opts: The entire population was strictly vegetarian by royal decree.
Meat eating was universal, and Buddhism mandated animal sacrifice.
The people generally abstained from meat, garlic, onions, and intoxicants, except for the Chandalas.
Wine and beef consumption was promoted by the court.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian observed that respectable, upper-caste, and non-Chandala citizens did not consume meat, onions, garlic, or intoxicants, and kept away from slaughterhouses, highlighting the strong moral and religious impact of Buddhism and rising Brahmanical values.

practiceQuestions.q: How did Faxian describe the social status and residential segregation of the 'Chandalas' in Gupta India?
opts: They lived inside city walls and shared equal rights with the nobility.
They were treated as untouchables, lived outside city limits, and had to strike a piece of wood as notice when entering towns.
They served as high-ranking ministers in Chandragupta II's royal council.
They were foreign merchants from Central Asia who enjoyed special tax concessions.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian provides one of the earliest clear foreign testimonies of untouchability, noting that Chandalas lived outside towns and were required to strike a piece of wood upon entering streets to warn people to avoid physical contact with them.

practiceQuestions.q: How does Faxian's account help modern historians evaluate the religious policy of the Gupta monarchs?
opts: It proves that the Gupta emperors actively persecuted Buddhism in favor of Vaishnavism.
It illustrates an era of remarkable religious tolerance, where Buddhism and Hinduism (Brahmanism) coexisted peacefully under royal patronage.
It shows that Buddhism had completely vanished from northern India by the 5th century CE.
It indicates that the state enforced secularism by banning religious institutions from holding land.
practiceQuestions.sol: Despite the Gupta rulers being devout Bhagavatas (Vaishnavites) who patronized Brahmanical Hinduism, Faxian's account reveals that Buddhism flourished with numerous monasteries, monks, and stupas receiving royal grants and protection, reflecting broad-based religious harmony.

practiceQuestions.q: Why do historians consider Faxian's silence on the political name of the reigning monarch (Chandragupta II) in his travelogue a significant curiosity or historiographical puzzle?
opts: Because Faxian was unaware that India had a king and believed it was governed by tribal councils.
Because his primary focus was exclusively monastic and spiritual, viewing worldly political rulers as insignificant compared to the Buddhist sangha.
Because Chandragupta II had ordered all references to his name to be erased from foreign texts.
Because the Gupta Empire had broken into petty principalities by the time Faxian arrived.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian was a monk on a sacred mission whose worldview was centred on the Dharma and monastic life. He describes the prosperous and peaceful administration of Central India (Madhya Pradesh/Madhya Desha) without ever mentioning the personal name of Emperor Chandragupta II, highlighting his distinct spiritual perspective.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the economic picture painted by Faxian contrast with the traditional Marxist interpretation of the Gupta period's later agrarian economy?
opts: Faxian describes a flourishing urban merchant network and free movement, whereas later periods saw feudal subjugation and tied labor.
Faxian noted total economic collapse and widespread famines across the Ganges valley.
Faxian highlights a state-monopolized socialist economy with zero private trade.
Faxian's account proves that coinage was completely replaced by barter trade.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian's descriptions of affluent cities like Pataliputra and Mathura, active merchant philanthropy, and easy personal mobility reflect the peak of urban prosperity during the early 5th century, serving as a baseline before the onset of feudal decentralization and sub-infeudation noted in later eras.

practiceQuestions.q: What inference can be drawn regarding the agricultural tax structure of the Gupta Empire based on Faxian's records?
opts: Peasants were heavily overburdened with punitive taxes and forced labor (Vishti).
Those who cultivate the royal land only pay a portion of the crop, reflecting a moderate revenue demand.
Agriculture was completely untaxed because the king derived revenue solely from foreign conquests.
All agricultural produce was confiscated by the state and redistributed through ration shops.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian noted that those who farmed royal crown lands paid a regulated portion of the produce as tax. The overall lightness of taxation matched the benevolent and non-oppressive character of Gupta administration.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are foreign accounts like Faxian's considered an indispensable supplement to indigenous literary and epigraphic sources for the Gupta period?
opts: Indigenous Gupta texts are completely silent on political history.
They offer an objective, outsider's perspective on the daily social life, moral standards, and economic realities of common people, uninfluenced by court panegyrics (prashastis).
Foreign accounts provide exact dynastic regnal dates that correct all errors in Indian stone inscriptions.
They are the only sources that mention the existence of Samudragupta and Chandragupta II.
None of the above
practiceQuestions.sol: While Gupta prashastis (like Allahabad Prasasti) and court literature praise kings in hyperbole, accounts like Faxian's 'Fo-Kuo-Ki' provide ground-level empirical observations on societal morality, hospital systems, market mechanisms, and popular customs.

practiceQuestions.q: How does Faxian's description of Pataliputra's monastic and secular institutions reflect the culmination of Mauryan legacy interacting with Gupta prosperity?
opts: It shows that Mauryan stone architecture was still standing and actively utilized or admired centuries later alongside vibrant Gupta-era charitable networks.
It proves that Pataliputra had been completely abandoned and replaced by Ujjain as the capital.
It indicates that Mauryan monuments were destroyed by Gupta rulers to build Hindu temples.
It reveals that Pataliputra had converted entirely to Jainism under royal influence.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian marveled at Asoka's palace in Pataliputra, believing it to be the work of supernatural beings due to its grand stonework, and noted the active presence of Mahayana and Hinayana monasteries functioning side by side with active public philanthropy.

practiceQuestions.q: What does Faxian's account of Indian monastic universities and stupas reveal about the transmission of Buddhist knowledge during the Gupta era?
opts: Buddhist texts were preserved solely in oral traditions with no written manuscripts.
Monks relied heavily on handwritten palm-leaf manuscripts and oral recitation traditions, prompting Faxian to spend years copying texts to take back to China.
Monasteries were banned from keeping libraries by imperial decree.
All Buddhist scriptures had already been translated into Chinese before Faxian arrived.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian’s primary struggle in India was finding authentic copies of the Vinaya Pitaka. He visited various centers like Mathura, Pataliputra, and Tamralipti, copying texts from palm-leaf manuscripts because they were largely transmitted orally or in regional scripts.

practiceQuestions.q: How did Faxian's travel route reflect the geo-political and trade connectivity between India and China during the early 5th century?
opts: He traveled overland through Central Asia and the Tarim Basin on his outward journey and returned to China via maritime routes through Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.
He flew directly from Chang'an to Pataliputra using imperial airships.
He used only the Himalayan mountain passes in both directions.
He sailed across the Pacific Ocean directly from the Bay of Bengal.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian's journey illustrates the vibrant dual-connectivity of the Silk Road network: overland through the treacherous deserts and mountain passes of Central Asia on his way to India, and via maritime trade routes from Tamralipti through Sri Lanka, Java, and the South China Sea on his return.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is Faxian's recording of the absence of state interference in personal lives considered a hallmark of the 'Golden Age' of the Guptas?
opts: It proves that the Gupta state was completely weak and unable to collect any taxes.
It indicates a high degree of civic freedom, economic abundance, and low crime rates that rendered heavy policing unnecessary.
It shows that society was anarchic with no laws governing property ownership.
It demonstrates that the emperor delegated all governance to foreign mercenaries.
practiceQuestions.sol: Faxian explicitly remarked on how people were not plagued by official inspections, forced requisitions, or rigid travel permits. This absence of petty tyranny by state officials points to efficient, prosperous governance characteristic of periods of high economic surplus.

practiceQuestions.q: How do Chinese accounts like Faxian's differ fundamentally in nature and focus from later Greek accounts (like Megasthenes' Indica)?
opts: Greek accounts were focused on religious monastic orders, whereas Chinese accounts focused strictly on military conquests.

Chinese accounts were deeply rooted in a religious and pilgrim perspective focusing on Buddhism, ethics, and sanghas, whereas Greek accounts were administrative and ethnographic descriptions written by royal ambassadors.
Chinese accounts were entirely fictional, whereas Greek accounts were scientific.
There is no difference; both were commissioned by the Mauryan court.
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes was a secular ambassador of Seleucus I Nikator focusing on Mauryan administration, military organization, and caste structure. Faxian, conversely, was a devout Buddhist pilgrim whose gaze was naturally drawn to the state of Buddhist teachings, monasteries, morality, and charitable institutions.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chinese pilgrim Faxian and his visit to India:
1. He visited India during the reign of the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II.
2. His primary objective was to collect authentic Buddhist texts, particularly the Vinaya Pitaka.
3. He entered India via the maritime route through the Bay of Bengal and returned overland through Central Asia.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
opts: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Faxian visited India during Chandragupta II's reign and came seeking authentic Buddhist texts like the Vinaya Pitaka. Statement 3 is incorrect because his outward journey was overland through Central Asia and the Taklamakan Desert, while his return journey was via maritime routes (Sea Route) through Sri Lanka and Java.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the socio-economic conditions of the Gupta Empire as reported by Faxian:
1. The administration was extremely strict with harsh physical punishments for petty thefts.
2. Cowries served as the common currency for daily retail transactions among common people.
3. Vegetarianism was widely practiced by upper-caste and respectable citizens.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Faxian explicitly noted that the Gupta administration was very lenient and mild, levying fines for minor offenses rather than brutal physical tortures or death penalties. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: cowries were used for retail trade, and vegetarianism along with abstinence from meat, garlic, and onions was prevalent among respectable citizens.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Faxian's observations on Buddhism in India:
1. Buddhism had completely disappeared from Mathura and Pataliputra by the time of his visit.
2. Monks belonging to both Hinayana and Mahayana schools were found residing peacefully in various monasteries.
3. Monasteries were heavily endowed with land grants and provisions by both royal patrons and wealthy merchants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Faxian found Mathura and Pataliputra to be major flourishing centers of Buddhism with numerous active monasteries and stupas. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: both Hinayana and Mahayana traditions coexisted, and monasteries received rich endowments of land, houses, gardens, and cattle from kings and wealthy householders.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the travelogues of foreign pilgrims during ancient India:
1. Faxian's account is titled 'Si-Yu-Ki'.
2. Xuanzang visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana in the 7th century CE.
3. Yijing provided detailed accounts of Buddhist monastic life and practices in the late 7th century.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
opts: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Faxian's travelogue is titled 'Fo-Kuo-Ki', whereas 'Si-Yu-Ki' is the title of Xuanzang's account. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Xuanzang came during Harshavardhana's rule in the 7th century, and Yijing (I-tsing) wrote extensively on monastic practices in India during the late 7th century.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Pataliputra as described by Faxian:
1. He described Asoka's palace in the city as having been constructed by spirits using supernatural powers due to its exquisite stonework.
2. He noted the presence of free hospitals established by benevolent citizens for the treatment of the poor and destitute.
3. He observed that the entire city had been completely abandoned and ruined following Mauryan collapse.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
opts: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Faxian was so awed by the stone masonry of Asoka's palace that he attributed it to divine/spiritual architects, and he praised the philanthropic free hospitals funded by local elites. Statement 3 is incorrect because Pataliputra was a vibrant, prosperous, and populated city during Faxian's visit.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding social hierarchy and restrictions in the Gupta Empire according to Faxian:
1. Untouchability was non-existent, and social mobility was fully fluid across all castes.
2. Chandalas lived outside the city limits and were required to make warning sounds by striking wood when entering public streets.
3. Citizens were required to carry royal travel permits and register with local police stations when moving between provinces.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 2 is correct: Faxian provides early evidence of untouchability, noting that Chandalas lived apart and warned people of their approach. Statement 1 is incorrect because rigid caste rules and untouchability were clearly present. Statement 3 is incorrect because Faxian noted that people could travel freely without passports or registration.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the economic life of the Gupta Empire based on foreign accounts:
1. Gold coins (dinaras) issued by Gupta kings were used primarily by common citizens for buying daily commodities like vegetables.
2. Inland and foreign trade flourished, with Tamralipti serving as a major port for maritime commerce with Southeast Asia and China.
3. Agriculture was heavily taxed, and peasants were subjected to forced bonded labor without compensation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
opts: 2 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 2 is correct: Tamralipti was indeed a major eastern port from which Faxian embarked on his return voyage to China, reflecting strong maritime links. Statement 1 is incorrect because gold dinaras were used for high-value transactions and royal gifts, while cowries were used for daily retail trade. Statement 3 is incorrect because taxation was generally moderate and light.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the historiographical significance of Faxian's writings:
1. Faxian explicitly mentions the personal name of the ruling emperor, Chandragupta II, in multiple chapters of his travelogue.
2. His account provides a valuable external verification of the peaceful and prosperous conditions prevalent in the Gupta heartland.
3. His work highlights the coexistence of Hinduism and Buddhism under a tolerant imperial administration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
opts: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Faxian never mentions the personal name of Chandragupta II in his travelogue, focusing purely on religious and societal conditions instead of secular political rulers. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: his text provides crucial external corroboration of Gupta peace, prosperity, and religious harmony.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Buddhist educational and monastic landscape in Gupta India as seen through Faxian's eyes:
1. Monasteries served merely as residential retirement homes for aged monks with no educational functions.
2. Monks engaged in rigorous study of sacred texts, meditation, and spiritual philosophy.
3. Major Buddhist centers of learning were supported by generous grants of land and revenue from the state and wealthy patrons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because monasteries were vibrant centers of learning, textual copying, debate, and spiritual instruction, not mere retirement homes. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: monks were deeply engaged in scriptural study and meditation, and these institutions were sustained by generous royal and merchant land grants.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the comparative aspects of Chinese travelers in ancient India:
1. Faxian traveled to India during the Gupta period, while Xuanzang arrived during the reign of Harshavardhana.
2. Both pilgrims shared the exact same itinerary across India and recorded identical observations about every city.
3. The primary motivation for both Faxian and Xuanzang was the acquisition and translation of authentic Buddhist scriptures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
opts: 1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Faxian visited during the Gupta epoch and Xuanzang during Harsha's era, and both were devout monks dedicated to acquiring Buddhist scriptures. Statement 2 is incorrect because their travel routes, specific regions visited, and observations differed significantly due to the changing political and social landscape over two centuries.
